_arch_note: ROW 3.3 OF THE LUT ABLATION: exp_g_0193 FORK testing the min_margin confidence form at a scale-matched gain. Forked VERBATIM from exp_g_0193_B16k_light_margin_tph128_noznorm_seed1 (LightMHL n=1, margin, no z_norm, H4 tph128 nap8 d_in=d_out=48, 6L d384 6 heads seq512, device_batch 12 x grad_accum 4 = 24,576 tokens, lr 3e-4, wd 0.1, warmup 0.1, seed 1, lut_base_seed 1000, tables_no_decay, untied, corrected eval bs48x100 skip-12, final 1.172852). CHANGES, exactly two: lut_confidence_form margin -> min_margin, i.e. score = (min_j |d_j|) * prod_j sigmoid(2|d_j|) instead of (sum_j |d_j|) * prod_j sigmoid(2|d_j|), which vanishes at every cell boundary and makes the n=1 forward continuous; and lut_confidence_gain 1.0 -> 37.4, the mean-score ratio margin:min_margin measured on exp_g_0193's own trained margins (doc/research/lut_ablation/min_margin_scale.py: 37.39 on 0193, 38.88 at init, 36.33 after 4K steps of sweep_s05), so the gate starts and stays at margin's scale. min_margin is NOT in the native scored-eval kernel: LightMHL._fused_eval refuses it, so no-grad eval uses the torch path (the same score code as training). CONFOUND: min_margin also roughly doubles within-token selectivity (CV ~1.7-2.0 vs ~0.9), so this arm alone cannot separate continuity from selectivity. References (corrected protocol): exp_g_0193 1.172852 (the direct control), exp_g_0195 1.160637 (n=2 learnable tau).
